summary:
Centre Alliance is a South Australian centrist and social liberal party that grew from Nick Xenophon’s independent political movement. Founded in 2013, it became the Nick Xenophon Team and adopted its current name in 2018, after withdrawing an application to become SA-BEST (Federal).

The party combines socially liberal and populist positions. Its members have supported same-sex marriage, climate action, intelligence-community reform, veterans, Australian manufacturing and legal euthanasia.

At the 2016 federal election, the Nick Xenophon Team won three Senate seats and Rebekha Sharkie’s House seat of Mayo. Xenophon left politics in 2017. The party won no new Senate seats in 2019, while Sharkie retained Mayo. In 2022, she was its only candidate and was re-elected. Senator Rex Patrick left in 2020, and Stirling Griff lost his seat in 2022.

By 2025, Sharkie was the party’s sole elected representative. She describes herself as “a party of one” and says she remains in Centre Alliance because of money held in its accounts.
